subject: sr-business-studies
title: Company Form of Business Organisation
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: A manager of a company signs a contract without using the common seal (where required). Who would be held legally liable?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a private company?
options: Can issue shares to the public
Requires a minimum capital of Rs 1 crore
questions.answer: C

questions.answer: A

questions.q: The smallest unit into which the capital of a company is divided is called —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The official signature of a joint stock company is its —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The minimum number of members to form a public company is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The maximum number of members in a private company (excluding employees) is —
questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the following with reference to a joint stock company: (a) The official signature of the company (b) The elected representatives of members who manage day-to-day affairs.
questions.answer: (a) Common seal. (b) Board of Directors.

questions.q: Identify the characteristic of a joint stock company: (a) Day-to-day management is done by elected representatives called the board of directors. (b) The company enjoys continuous existence.
questions.answer: (a) Distinct pattern of management. (b) Perpetual succession.

questions.q: Give the minimum number of members required: (i) public company (ii) private company.
questions.answer: (i) Seven. (ii) Two.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) A private company can invite the public to subscribe to its shares. (ii) A company has perpetual succession.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: A private company must write ______ at the end of its name; a public company must write ______.
questions.answer: Private Limited; Limited.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) A statutory corporation's capital is provided wholly by the government. (ii) A government company is incorporated under a special Act of Parliament.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – under the Companies Act.

questions.q: Match: (i) Memorandum of Association (ii) Articles of Association (iii) Certificate of Incorporation with (a) internal rules (b) birth certificate (c) charter of the company's objects.
Name the form of organisation: (a) maximum flexibility, secrecy (b) can raise huge capital and hire expert knowledge.
questions.answer: (a) Sole proprietorship. (b) Joint stock company.

questions.q: Give the full form: (a) CIN (b) OPC.
questions.answer: (a) Corporate Identity Number. (b) One Person Company.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Define a 'small company' according to Section 2(85) of the Companies Act 2013.
questions.answer: A company other than a public company with paid-up share capital not exceeding Rs 50 lakh and turnover not exceeding Rs 2 crore.

questions.q: Define a 'public company' according to Section 2(71) of the Companies Act 2013.
questions.answer: A company which is not a private company and has the prescribed minimum paid-up share capital.

questions.q: What is a Public-Private Partnership form of organisation? State one feature.
questions.answer: A partnership between the public and private sectors in financing and developing infrastructure; feature: risk and responsibility are shared between the two.

questions.q: What is a one-person company (OPC)? State one feature.
questions.answer: A company with only one person as its member; feature: no need to hold an Annual General Meeting.

questions.q: State any two differences between a public company and a private company.
questions.answer: A public company needs minimum seven members and freely transfers shares and invites the public; a private company needs two members, restricts share transfer and cannot invite the public.

questions.q: Explain briefly any two limitations of government companies.
questions.answer: Government interference and political influence reduce autonomy; excessive formalities and delay in decisions.

questions.q: Why were public enterprises started? Explain.
questions.answer: To prevent concentration of economic power, develop infrastructure and basic industries, ensure equitable distribution, create employment and achieve balanced regional growth.

questions.q: What is a joint venture? Give an example.
questions.answer: A business in which two or more independent firms contribute capital and participate in operations; Maruti Suzuki.

questions.q: State two features of a statutory corporation.
questions.answer: It is incorporated under a special Act of Parliament and is autonomous in internal management with capital provided by the government.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Give any three features of a private company.
questions.answer: Restricts the transfer of shares; limits members to 200 and needs minimum two; prohibits invitation to the public to subscribe to its securities (and adds 'Private Limited' to its name).

questions.q: Give any three features of a public company.
questions.answer: Can invite the public to subscribe to shares; minimum seven members with no maximum; free transfer of shares; 'Limited' in its name.

questions.q: Explain the merits of a joint stock company (any three).
questions.answer: Large resources, limited liability and continuity of existence; also professional management and tax benefits.

questions.q: Explain the limitations of a joint stock company (any three).
questions.answer: Difficult to form, control by a group, excessive government control, delay in decisions and lack of secrecy.

questions.q: Explain the registration stage of company formation.
questions.answer: Documents such as Memorandum, Articles, list of directors, consent of directors and statutory declaration are filed with the Registrar who issues a Certificate of Incorporation and a CIN.

questions.q: Explain the features of a multinational corporation.
questions.answer: Centralised management, worldwide spread, better quality, large size, access to the international market and special attention to advertisement.

questions.q: Explain the features of a departmental undertaking.
questions.answer: Established by the government and controlled by a minister, part of the government, financed from the budget, subject to budgetary accounting and audit, accountable to the legislature.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any five limitations of a joint stock company.
questions.answer: Difficult formation, control by a few directors or families, excessive government control, delay in decision making, lack of secrecy and social abuses such as monopoly and exploitation.

questions.q: Explain any five factors that should be kept in mind while choosing a form of business.
questions.answer: Ease of formation, availability of large resources, liability or risk, stability, flexibility, secrecy and extent of state control.

questions.q: Differentiate between public enterprises and private enterprises on the basis of any five points.
questions.answer: Objective (welfare versus profit), ownership (government versus individuals), management (government versus owners and professionals), capital (government funds versus owners' funds and public issues), area of operation (basic and public utility versus all areas).

questions.q: Explain the stages in the formation of a company.
questions.answer: Promotion (idea and action by promoters), registration (documents filed and Certificate of Incorporation and CIN), capital subscription and commencement of business (permitted immediately after incorporation since 2015).

questions.q: Explain the forms of public sector enterprises.
questions.answer: Departmental undertakings (run by a ministry), statutory corporations (set up by special Acts, autonomous) and government companies (51 per cent or more government shareholding under the Companies Act), with merits and limitations.
